title: Ten-client compatibility matrix
description: Closed record of one bounded compatibility assessment run across every installed coding-agent client. Each client carries four independently recorded stage results — placement, discovery, load, invocation — followed by exactly one overall status. Ten rows are not ten assessments: a row that stops at its first failure and reports one status proves nothing about whether the package ever loaded, so every stage is recorded even when an earlier stage already failed. This record is published in a public repository and therefore carries field names, counts, and digests rather than raw discovered inventory: no address, hostname, hardware address, or credential value may appear in any command, evidence, or reason string.

schema_version.description: 1 records one command per stage. 2 additionally records every command a stage ran beside that command's own exit status, so a multi-command stage is reproducible and a reader can tell which command returned which status.

assessed_on.description: Calendar date of the assessment run, ISO-8601.

package.description: The package under assessment, identified by digest rather than by content.

tree_sha256.description: Digest over the sorted per-file digests of the assessed tree.

method.description: What was held identical across all ten clients, so the rows are comparable.

clients.description: Exactly the ten installed clients, asserted by set equality against the canonical list rather than by count, so a substituted or renamed client cannot pass as covered.

stages.description: All four stages are mandatory. A row missing a stage fails the check even when it carries an overall status.

status.description: Exactly one overall status. Unsupported and failed are accepted outcomes: coverage is mandatory, passing is not.

command.description: Required when the result is executed. Site-identifying arguments are redacted to a placeholder before the command is recorded.

evidence.description: Required when the result is executed. What the client reported, as field names, counts, and comparisons rather than raw output.

reason.description: Required when the result is blocked or not applicable.

commands.description: Schema version 2. Every command the stage executed, in order, each with its own exit status. `command` remains the first of these. Site-identifying arguments are redacted to a placeholder before a command is recorded.
